body.x: AVING USA, a global technology and business outlet, named MOBILTECH, AIRC Inc. and YOUNG HYUN ROBOTICS Co., Ltd. its top three innovative companies at the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards.

The Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026) ran from Oct. 21 to Oct. 24 at EXCO in Daegu, featuring future mobility, robotics, and AI and ICT technologies and products. In the Global Media Awards, overseas outlets review technologies and products on the show floor, and each outlet chooses its own top three companies.

AVING News covers major exhibitions and industrial sites around the world through its global news network and introduces Korean companies' technology and products to overseas markets. It co-hosted the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards with its global media partners, helping to publicize domestic companies' technology to the world.

Explaining the selection criteria, Davis Kim, director of AVING USA's U.S. branch, said, "We paid attention to companies that broke through an industry's stagnation with technology, or showed creativity in applying technology to unexpected fields."

The three companies AVING USA chose show new uses of technology in different areas: spatial data and digital twin technology that supports autonomous driving and robot development, a robot automation-based unmanned retail solution, and the extension of industrial robot technology into services.
MOBILTECH Builds the Base for Physical AI With Spatial Data and Digital Twins

MOBILTECH is a spatial intelligence and physical AI infrastructure company that helps autonomous vehicles and robots perceive and understand the real world. Its technology runs from sensor data collection and calibration to 3D mapping and building high-precision digital twins, and supports the development, simulation and verification of autonomous driving and robotics systems.

Its main solutions include Sensor Suite, which collects and fuses multi-sensor data; Calib Suite, which supports inspection and calibration of sensor data; and Replica City, which builds virtual spaces based on high-precision digital twins. With them, real-world spatial information is converted into data, and various simulations and verification can be run in virtual environments.

For autonomous vehicles and robots to operate reliably in real environments, they must precisely combine information from sensors such as cameras and LiDAR and accurately grasp the structure and characteristics of the surrounding space. Simulation technology that can verify the situations likely to arise in real environments during development is also important.

MOBILTECH's solutions provide a development base running from sensor data acquisition through calibration and spatial modeling to digital twin construction. Because they turn the real world into precise data and use it in developing and verifying autonomous driving and robotics systems, they draw attention as base technology for the physical AI era.

Through MOBILTECH, AVING USA looked at the importance of the base technology that lets robots and autonomous vehicles perceive and operate in the real world, beyond the machines themselves. It is a case that shows the technical foundation of the future mobility industry by tying together the data and spatial intelligence technology needed behind the visible movement of AI into a single development process.
AIRC Redesigns Retail Sales and Store Operation With Robot Automation

AIRC Inc. develops an AI unmanned robot convenience store solution that uses robot automation to store and dispense products. The unmanned convenience store built on its PnGO platform differs from the existing self-checkout approach, in which customers pick products inside the store and pay, by using automated equipment to dispense products.

AIRC presents on its official website and FAQ an unmanned convenience store model optimized for a space of about 33 square meters (10 pyeong). According to the company, it is designed to sell about 1,500 products in a store of that size. This is the operating standard the company has published, and actual product mix and operating results may vary with store environment and adoption conditions.

Existing unmanned stores face challenges in managing theft and damage, checking inventory and running the store efficiently, since customers select products and pay on their own. AIRC changes the way products reach customers by automating storage and dispensing with robots, aiming to make store operation and product management easier.

The approach does more than automate payment: it redesigns how a store stores and sells products. Trying to handle a wide range of products in a limited space while automating product management and dispensing suggests a way to expand the operating model of small unmanned sales spaces.

AVING USA included AIRC in its top three because the company applies robot technology to an everyday consumer space outside the factory. It is a case showing that robot automation can change retail operations and the customer experience, not just raise efficiency at production sites.
YOUNG HYUN ROBOTICS Extends Collaborative Robots From Industrial Sites to Everyday Services

YOUNG HYUN ROBOTICS Co., Ltd. is a robot company whose product lineup, built on collaborative robot technology, includes humanoids, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), food and beverage automation robots, everyday service robots and robot parts. It is extending robot technology used at industrial sites beyond manufacturing processes into retail, food and beverage, and everyday services.

A collaborative robot is designed to perform a variety of tasks in the same workspace as people and is used for flexible production environments and process automation. Building on this technology, YOUNG HYUN ROBOTICS has presented products and applied solutions that automate repetitive work and support service operations.

At FIX 2026, it widened the range of robot uses with an ice cream robot and a cellulite care robot, among others. Robots in food and beverage can be applied to making and serving products by repeating fixed motions, and robots in everyday services can raise user convenience by automating specific functions. The company also presents related lineups such as humanoids, AMRs and robot parts.

To apply industrial robot technology to various service areas, a robot's motions, control methods and safety requirements have to be designed differently for each work environment and purpose. By extending the robot technology required in manufacturing to food and beverage, retail and everyday services, YOUNG HYUN ROBOTICS is widening the areas where robot automation can apply.

AVING USA's selection of YOUNG HYUN ROBOTICS reflects its attempt to bring robot technology into daily life and service settings rather than keeping it to specific manufacturing processes. Its approach of widening the boundary between industrial and service robots to automate varied tasks shows how robot technology is being used in real life and at industrial sites.
Base Technology for AI That Understands the Real World

AVING USA's top three, chosen for creativity in breaking through an industry's limits with technology or applying it in new fields, span spatial data and digital twins, unmanned retail automation, and industrial and service robots. MOBILTECH provides spatial intelligence infrastructure that helps autonomous driving and robots perceive the real world, AIRC redesigns how products are sold and how stores operate through robot automation, and YOUNG HYUN ROBOTICS extends industrial robot technology into everyday life and services.

The three cases show that innovation does not necessarily come from inventing entirely new technology. Solving problems an existing industry faces with new technology, or applying already accumulated technology to another field to create new uses, is also an important innovation strategy.

As AI and robotics technology spread to real industry and daily life, the technology's performance matters, and so do its practicality in real environments, how it is operated and how it connects to existing systems. The top three are notable as attempts by companies to tie technology to specific industrial problems amid this change.

Ten global media outlets from Europe, the Americas and Asia took part in the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards. Each outlet reviewed the technologies and products of exhibiting companies and chose its own top three. Selected companies gain an opportunity to be publicized through overseas media.

The press corps included Leo Thevenet, editor-in-chief of Le Café du Geek, an IT, lifestyle and global technology outlet; Juan Castromil, editor-in-chief of Clipset, a Spanish mobile and consumer electronics outlet; Eliane Fiolet, editor-in-chief of Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley outlet covering IT and consumer electronics innovation; Davis Kim, reporter at AVING USA, a global technology, business and exhibition outlet; Yoshioka Tomomi, editor-in-chief of Otaku Soken, a Japanese outlet covering subculture and AI, virtual reality and IT convergence technology; Sherri Wang, research editor at DIGITIMES, a global outlet covering semiconductor and ICT supply chains; Võ Hoàng Long, reporter and deputy editor-in-chief of VietnamPlus, a Vietnamese state-run general news portal; Stephanie Chen, editor-in-chief of ChinaByte, a Chinese outlet covering IT, enterprise digital transformation (DX) and AI; Dimpal Bajwa, deputy editor of ET Manufacturing, an Indian outlet covering smart factories, robotics and manufacturing technology; and Mubashar Aftab, founder and publisher of Pokde.Net, a Malaysian outlet covering IT hardware, gaming and mobile technology.

The media partners took part in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day and in on-site judging for the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards during the show, and covered firsthand news from innovative companies set to lead Korea's future industries, introducing it to readers around the world.
